answer: Forging 395 aliases thus costs 169 bonds held for 4 days each, plus the ocean attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a jade, before it can post or attest. A single spiral checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
